title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception

reading.body:
An AI system was used to generate a fake news article containing a fabricated interview between real public figures discussing a fraudulent cryptocurrency platform. The article claimed events that never occurred and presented them as fact. This deployment had no human verification step, either before publication or as part of the platform's moderation process for financial content.

The failure was impersonation at scale. Scammers used AI to create realistic-looking false endorsements and fake news to promote unlicensed investment schemes. The system was deployed in a domain where accuracy is critical and verification is feasible, but was apparently not checked against public records or the actual schedules and statements of the people being impersonated. ASIC reports the trend is accelerating, with a 182 percent year-on-year increase in such schemes.

It is not established how the AI systems were built, trained, or instructed to generate this specific content, or what controls, if any, were present in the platforms that hosted and distributed it.

reports.title: The fake Alan Kohler interview that shows a type of scam that’s on the rise
AI deepfake scams 'an emergency in the making' as ASIC reports rise in false investment endorsements
ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception

summary:
A fake online article featured a fabricated interview between ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock discussing Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The article claimed Bullock stormed out during heated questioning, but this interview never actually occurred. This scam represents a growing trend where artificial intelligence generates deepfake content to promote fraudulent investments.

Australia's corporate regulator ASIC reports a significant surge in AI-powered investment scams, removing 19,400 schemes last year, a 182 percent increase. Scammers create elaborate deceptions using fake news articles, fabricated quotes, and impersonations of well-known figures including Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Alan Kohler, and billionaire Gina Rinehart. ASIC urges consumers to verify financial services licenses independently and check company details against ASIC's public registers before investing. The regulator is increasing enforcement efforts while Kohler argues platforms carrying such content should face heavy fines.
